01
Before the first verse · Vol. 3, p. 141

Opening of the surah

Vol. 3, p. 141
Sūrat al-Ḥajj is Meccan, except for six verses, namely: "These are two adversaries..." up to His saying "...to the path of the Praiseworthy." It has seventy-eight verses. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
سورة الحج مكية، غيرست آيات، وهي: هذان خصمان … إلى قوله … إلى صراط الحميد وهي ثمان وسبعون آية بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 141
1. (1). His statement "that the slipping of things be intensified": that is, the displacement of things and their moving away from their places is repeated. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "You say zalaltu, O so-and-so (with a fatḥa), tazillu zalīlan, when someone slips in mud or in speech." (ʿ) [.....]
2. . Thus al-Thaʿlabī and al-Baghawī mention it. They said: "It is reported on the authority of ʿImrān b. Ḥuṣayn, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and others that these two verses were revealed at night during the expedition against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq," to the end. I say: it is a composite stitched together from the two reports mentioned, and the third is Ibn ʿAbbās, in what Ibn Isḥāq related from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "While the Messenger of God ﷺ was on the march during the expedition against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, there was revealed to him 'O people, fear your Lord...' up to '...but the punishment of God is severe.' He halted upon his she-camel and raised his voice," (the ḥadīth). It was also related by al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and al-Ḥākim by the route of al-Ḥasan from ʿImrān b. Ḥuṣayn: "that the Messenger of God ﷺ in one of his journeys, when his companions had drawn close to one another in travel, raised his voice with these two verses, 'O people, fear your Lord...' up to His saying 'but the punishment of God is severe.' When his companions heard this they urged on their mounts, and knew that he had something to say. When they gathered around him he said: 'Do you know which day that is? It is the day on which Adam is called,'" (the ḥadīth). In it: "His companions were struck dumb, until none of them showed a smile. When he saw that he said: 'Know this and rejoice,'" (the ḥadīth). As for its ending, I have not seen it.
1. (1) . قوله «وأن يضاعف زليل الأشياء» أى يكرر انحراف الأشياء وتزحزحها عن مواضعها. وفي الصحاح: تقول زللت يا فلان- بالفتح- تزل زليلا: إذا زل في طين أو منطق. (ع) [.....]
2. . هكذا ذكره الثعلبي والبغوي. قالا: روى عن عمران بن حصين وأبى سعيد الخدري وغيرهما أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا ليلا في غزوة بنى المصطلق إلى آخره» قلت: وهو ملفق من حديثيه المذكورين. وثالثهما ابن عباس فيما رواه ابن إسحاق عن الكلبي عن أبى صالح عن ابن عباس قال «بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسيره في غزوة بنى المصطلق إذ نزل عليه يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ- إلى- شَدِيدٌ فوقف على ناقته، ورفع صوته- الحديث، ورواه الترمذي والنسائي والحاكم من طريق الحسن عن عمران بن حصين «أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في بعض أسفاره وقد تقارب من أصحابه السير ورفع بهاتين صوته يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ- إلى قوله: وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ فلما سمع أصحابه بذلك حثوا المطىّ وعرفوا أنه عنده قول يقوله، فلما التفوا حوله قال: أتدرون أى يوم ذلك؟ يوم ينادى آدم- الحديث. وفيه: فأبلس أصحابه حتى ما أوضحوا بضاحكة. فلما رأى ذلك قال: اعلموا وأبشروا- الحديث» وأما آخره فلم أره.
02
Q 22:1 · Vol. 3, pp. 141–142

Verse 1

The verse as the commentary quotes it
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. "O people, fear your Lord. Indeed, the quaking of the Hour is a tremendous thing." (1)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ شَيْءٌ عَظِيمٌ (1)
Vol. 3, p. 141
Al-zalzala is intense shaking and disturbance, namely that the slipping of things (1) from their places and fixed positions is repeated and intensified. The Hour (al-sāʿa) must be taken in one of two ways. Either it is construed as the agent of the quaking, as though the Hour itself were what shakes things, by way of figurative attribution to the agent, so that the quaking is a verbal noun annexed to its agent; or it is construed as the locus in which the quaking occurs, by way of extension in the adverbial of time, treating it like a direct object, as in His saying, Exalted is He, "Rather, it is the scheming of night and day." It is the quaking mentioned in His saying, "When the earth is shaken with its [final] quaking." There is disagreement about its time. Al-Ḥasan reports that it will occur on the Day of Resurrection, while ʿAlqama and al-Shaʿbī say that it will occur at the rising of the sun from its place of setting. He commanded the children of Adam to be God-fearing, then gave as the ground of its being obligatory upon them the mention of the Hour, describing it with the most terrifying description, so that they might look upon that description with their inner eyes and picture it with their minds, until they spare themselves and have mercy on themselves from the horrors of that Day, by carrying out what their Lord commanded them, namely to wrap themselves in the garment of God-fearing, which alone will give them security from those terrors if they wrap themselves in it. It is reported that these two verses were revealed at night during the expedition against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq; the Messenger of God ﷺ recited them, and no one was seen weeping more than they were that night. When morning came, they did not take the saddles off the beasts, did not pitch the tents when they halted, and did not cook a pot, for they were divided among the grieving, the weeping, and the deeply pensive (2).
الزلزلة: شدّة التحريك والإزعاج، وأن يضاعف زليل الأشياء «1» عن مقارّها ومراكزها ولا تخلو السَّاعَةِ من أن تكون على تقدير الفاعلة لها، كأنها هي التي تزلزل الأشياء على المجاز الحكمي، فتكون الزلزلة مصدرا مضافا إلى فاعله. أو على تقدير المفعول فيها على طريقة الاتساع في الظرف وإجرائه مجرى المفعول به، كقوله تعالى بَلْ مَكْرُ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ وهي الزلزلة المذكورة في قوله إِذا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزالَها واختلف في وقتها، فعن الحسن أنها تكون يوم القيامة وعن علقمة والشعبي: عند طلوع الشمس من مغربها. أمر بنى آدم بالتقوى، ثم علل وجوبها عليهم بذكر الساعة ووصفها بأهول صفة، لينظروا إلى تلك الصفة ببصائرهم ويتصوّروها بعقولهم، حتى يبقوا على أنفسهم ويرحموها من شدائد ذلك اليوم، بامتثال ما أمرهم به ربهم من التردي بلباس التقوى، الذي لا يؤمنهم من تلك الأفزاع إلا أن يتردوا به. وروى أنّ هاتين الآيتين نزلتا ليلا في غزوة بنى المصطلق، فقرأهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم ير أكثر باكيا من تلك الليلة، فلما أصبحوا لم يحطوا السروج عن الدواب، ولم يضربوا الخيام وقت النزول، ولم يطبخوا قدرا، وكانوا من بين حزين وباك ومفكر «2»
Vol. 3, p. 142

1. (1) . قوله «وأن يضاعف زليل الأشياء» أى يكرر انحراف الأشياء وتزحزحها عن مواضعها. وفي الصحاح: تقول زللت يا فلان- بالفتح- تزل زليلا: إذا زل في طين أو منطق. (ع) [.....]
2. . هكذا ذكره الثعلبي والبغوي. قالا: روى عن عمران بن حصين وأبى سعيد الخدري وغيرهما أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا ليلا في غزوة بنى المصطلق إلى آخره» قلت: وهو ملفق من حديثيه المذكورين. وثالثهما ابن عباس فيما رواه ابن إسحاق عن الكلبي عن أبى صالح عن ابن عباس قال «بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسيره في غزوة بنى المصطلق إذ نزل عليه يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ- إلى- شَدِيدٌ فوقف على ناقته، ورفع صوته- الحديث، ورواه الترمذي والنسائي والحاكم من طريق الحسن عن عمران بن حصين «أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في بعض أسفاره وقد تقارب من أصحابه السير ورفع بهاتين صوته يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ- إلى قوله: وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ فلما سمع أصحابه بذلك حثوا المطىّ وعرفوا أنه عنده قول يقوله، فلما التفوا حوله قال: أتدرون أى يوم ذلك؟ يوم ينادى آدم- الحديث. وفيه: فأبلس أصحابه حتى ما أوضحوا بضاحكة. فلما رأى ذلك قال: اعلموا وأبشروا- الحديث» وأما آخره فلم أره.
Vol. 3, p. 142
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "One says murḍiʿ on the basis of relation (nasab), and murḍiʿa on the basis of the original form of the active participle." Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: The difference between them is that when it occurs on the basis of relation, no attention is paid to the occurrence of the attribute from which it is derived; its import is only that the person is described by it. When it is not on the basis of relation, attention is paid to the occurrence of the act and the attribute's proceeding from it. So it is in the verse, because of His saying "from what she nursed," where He made the attribute proceed from the act and attached the tāʾ to it.
2. . His statement "or your being seen standing": perhaps it should be: "or you were seen standing." (ʿ)
3. . Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "His saying 'and you will see the people intoxicated though they are not intoxicated': He first affirmed for them a figurative intoxication, then denied of them real intoxication." Aḥmad said: The scholars say that one of the proofs of figurative usage is that its contradictory can truthfully be asserted, as when you say "Zayd is a donkey," describing him as dull-witted, and it is then also true to say "he is not a donkey," denying real identity. Likewise in the verse, after affirming figurative intoxication, He denies the reality, with the most emphatic denial, strengthened with the bāʾ. The secret of its emphasis is to draw attention to the fact that this intoxication they are in, in that state, is nothing of the familiar kind; it is something of which they had never known the like before. The contrastive "but" in His saying "but the punishment of God is severe" goes back to His saying "though they are not intoxicated," and is as though it were a justification for affirming the figurative intoxication, as if it were said: "If they are not drunk from wine, which is the familiar intoxication, then what is this strange intoxication and what is its cause?" So He said: its cause is the severity of the punishment of God, Exalted is He. It is also reported from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq ؓ that he said: "It is the time at which each of the prophets, peace be upon them, says: 'Myself, myself!'"
1. (1) . قال محمود: «يقال مرضع على النسب ومرضعة على أصل اسم الفاعل» قال أحمد: والفرق بينهما أن وروده على النسب لا يلاحظ فيه حدوث الصفة المشتق منها، ولكن مقتضاه أنه موصوف بها، وعلى غير النسب يلاحظ حدوث الفعل وخروج الصفة عليه، وكذلك هو في الآية لقوله عَمَّا أَرْضَعَتْ فأخرج الصفة على الفعل، وألحقه التاء.
2. . قوله «أو رؤيتك قائما» لعله: أو رؤيت قائما. (ع)
3. . قال محمود: «وقوله وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى: أثبت لهم أولا السكر المجازى، ثم نفى عنهم السكر الحقيقي» قال أحمد: والعلماء يقولون: إن من أدلة المجاز صدق نقيضه، كقولك: زيد حمار، إذا وصفته بالبلادة، ثم يصدق أن تقول: وما هو بحمار، فتنفى عنه الحقيقة، فكذلك الآية بعد أن أثبت السكر المجازى نفى الحقيقة أبلغ نفى مؤكد بالباء. والسر في تأكيده: التنبيه على أن هذا السكر الذي هو بهم في تلك الحالة ليس من المعهود في شيء، وإنما هو أمر لم يعهدوا قبله مثله، والاستدراك بقوله وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ راجع إلى قوله وَما هُمْ بِسُكارى وكأنه تعليل لاثبات السكر المجازى، كأنه قيل: إذا لم يكونوا سكارى من الخمر وهو السكر المعهود، فما هذا السكر الغريب وما سببه؟ فقال: سببه شدة عذاب الله تعالى، ونقل عن جعفر بن محمد الصادق رضى الله عنه أنه قال: هو الوقت الذي يقول كل من الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام فيه «نفسي نفسي» .
03
Q 22:2 · Vol. 3, pp. 142–143

Verse 2

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she nursed, and every pregnant female will deliver her burden, and you will see the people intoxicated though they are not intoxicated, but the punishment of God is severe." (2)
يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَها تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمَّا أَرْضَعَتْ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَها وَتَرَى النَّاسَ سُكارى وَما هُمْ بِسُكارى وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ (2)
Vol. 3, p. 142
"The Day you see it" is in the accusative, governed by "will be distracted" (tadhhalu), and the pronoun refers to the quaking. It has also been read: "Every nursing mother will be made distracted" (tudhhalu), in the passive voice, that is, the quaking will make her distracted. Dhuhūl is the departing from a matter in a state of bewilderment.
يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَها منصوب بتذهل. والضمير للزلزلة. وقرئ: تذهل كل مرضعة، على البناء للمفعول: وتذهل كل مرضعة أى: تذهلها الزلزلة. والذهول: الذهاب عن الأمر مع دهشة.
Question
If you ask: why was it said murḍiʿa (with the tāʾ) and not murḍiʿ?
فإن قلت: لم قيل مُرْضِعَةٍ دون مرضع؟
Answer
I say: the murḍiʿa is the woman who is in the very act of nursing, her breast placed in the infant's mouth, whereas the murḍiʿ is the woman whose characteristic it is to nurse even if she is not engaged in nursing at the time she is so described (1). So it was said murḍiʿa to indicate that, when this terror suddenly befalls such a woman while she has placed her breast in the nursling's mouth, she will tear it away from his mouth because of the bewilderment that seizes her. "From what she nursed" means: from her nursing, or from the one she nursed, namely the child. Al-Ḥasan said: the nursing mother will be distracted from her child though it has not been weaned, and the pregnant woman will deliver what is in her belly though it has not come to term. "And you will see" (tarā) has been read with a ḍamma (turā), from "I made you see (urīka) standing" or "your being seen standing" (2). "The people" (al-nās) is either accusative or nominative. The accusative is plain. As for the one who reads it as nominative, he makes al-nās the subject of turā, and makes the verb feminine on the sense of "a group." It has also been read sakrā and bi-sakrā, which parallels jūʿā and ʿaṭshā for jawʿān and ʿaṭshān; and sukārā and bi-sukārā, like kusālā and ʿujālā. From al-Aʿmash: sukrā and bi-sukrā with a ḍamma, which is unusual. The meaning is: you see them as drunk by way of simile, but they are not drunk in reality (3), rather what has overtaken them of the fear of God's punishment is what has taken away
قلت: المرضعة التي هي في حال الإرضاع ملقمة ثديها الصبى. والمرضع: التي شأنها أن ترضع وإن لم تباشر الإرضاع في حال وصفها به «1» فقيل: مرضعة، ليدل على أن ذلك الهول إذا فوجئت به هذه وقد ألقمت الرضيع ثديها نزعته عن فيه لما يلحقها من الدهشة عَمَّا أَرْضَعَتْ عن إرضاعها، أو عن الذي أرضعته وهو الطفل وعن الحسن: تذهل المرضعة عن ولدها لغير فطام، وتضع الحامل ما في بطنها لغير تمام. قرئ وَتَرَى بالضم من أريتك قائما. أو رؤيتك قائما» . والنَّاسَ منصوب ومرفوع، والنصب ظاهر. ومن رفع جعل الناس اسم ترى، وأنثه على تأويل الجماعة. وقرئ: سكرى. وبسكرى، وهو نظير: جوعى وعطشى، في جوعان وعطشان. وسكارى وبسكارى، نحو كسالى وعجالى. وعن الأعمش: سكرى، وبسكرى، بالضم، وهو غريب. والمعنى: وتراهم سكارى على التشبيه، وما هم بسكارى على التحقيق «3» ولكن ما رهقهم من خوف عذاب الله هو الذي أذهب
Vol. 3, p. 143
their minds, scattered their discernment, and brought them back to something like the condition of one whose mind and discernment intoxication has carried off. It is also said: "You see them drunk with fear, though they are not drunk with drink."
عقولهم وطير تمييزهم وردّهم في نحو حال من يذهب السكر بعقله وتمييزه. وقيل وتراهم سكارى من الخوف، وما هم بسكارى من الشراب.
Question
If you ask: why was it first said "you see" in the plural (tarawna), and then "you see" (tarā) in the singular?
فإن قلت: لم قيل أوّلا: ترون، ثم قيل: ترى، على الإفراد؟
Answer
I say: because the seeing at first was attached to the quaking, so all the people were made to be seeing it; but at the end it is attached to the people being in the state of intoxication, so each one of them must necessarily be made to be seeing the rest.
قلت: لأنّ الرؤية أوّلا علقت بالزلزلة فجعل الناس جميعا رائين لها، وهي معلقة أخيرا بكون الناس على حال السكر، فلا بد أن يجعل كل واحد منهم رائيا لسائرهم.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 142
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "One says murḍiʿ on the basis of relation (nasab), and murḍiʿa on the basis of the original form of the active participle." Aḥmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: The difference between them is that when it occurs on the basis of relation, no attention is paid to the occurrence of the attribute from which it is derived; its import is only that the person is described by it. When it is not on the basis of relation, attention is paid to the occurrence of the act and the attribute's proceeding from it. So it is in the verse, because of His saying "from what she nursed," where He made the attribute proceed from the act and attached the tāʾ to it.
2. . His statement "or your being seen standing": perhaps it should be: "or you were seen standing." (ʿ)
3. . Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "His saying 'and you will see the people intoxicated though they are not intoxicated': He first affirmed for them a figurative intoxication, then denied of them real intoxication." Aḥmad said: The scholars say that one of the proofs of figurative usage is that its contradictory can truthfully be asserted, as when you say "Zayd is a donkey," describing him as dull-witted, and it is then also true to say "he is not a donkey," denying real identity. Likewise in the verse, after affirming figurative intoxication, He denies the reality, with the most emphatic denial, strengthened with the bāʾ. The secret of its emphasis is to draw attention to the fact that this intoxication they are in, in that state, is nothing of the familiar kind; it is something of which they had never known the like before. The contrastive "but" in His saying "but the punishment of God is severe" goes back to His saying "though they are not intoxicated," and is as though it were a justification for affirming the figurative intoxication, as if it were said: "If they are not drunk from wine, which is the familiar intoxication, then what is this strange intoxication and what is its cause?" So He said: its cause is the severity of the punishment of God, Exalted is He. It is also reported from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq ؓ that he said: "It is the time at which each of the prophets, peace be upon them, says: 'Myself, myself!'"
1. (1) . قال محمود: «يقال مرضع على النسب ومرضعة على أصل اسم الفاعل» قال أحمد: والفرق بينهما أن وروده على النسب لا يلاحظ فيه حدوث الصفة المشتق منها، ولكن مقتضاه أنه موصوف بها، وعلى غير النسب يلاحظ حدوث الفعل وخروج الصفة عليه، وكذلك هو في الآية لقوله عَمَّا أَرْضَعَتْ فأخرج الصفة على الفعل، وألحقه التاء.
2. . قوله «أو رؤيتك قائما» لعله: أو رؤيت قائما. (ع)
3. . قال محمود: «وقوله وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى: أثبت لهم أولا السكر المجازى، ثم نفى عنهم السكر الحقيقي» قال أحمد: والعلماء يقولون: إن من أدلة المجاز صدق نقيضه، كقولك: زيد حمار، إذا وصفته بالبلادة، ثم يصدق أن تقول: وما هو بحمار، فتنفى عنه الحقيقة، فكذلك الآية بعد أن أثبت السكر المجازى نفى الحقيقة أبلغ نفى مؤكد بالباء. والسر في تأكيده: التنبيه على أن هذا السكر الذي هو بهم في تلك الحالة ليس من المعهود في شيء، وإنما هو أمر لم يعهدوا قبله مثله، والاستدراك بقوله وَلكِنَّ عَذابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ راجع إلى قوله وَما هُمْ بِسُكارى وكأنه تعليل لاثبات السكر المجازى، كأنه قيل: إذا لم يكونوا سكارى من الخمر وهو السكر المعهود، فما هذا السكر الغريب وما سببه؟ فقال: سببه شدة عذاب الله تعالى، ونقل عن جعفر بن محمد الصادق رضى الله عنه أنه قال: هو الوقت الذي يقول كل من الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام فيه «نفسي نفسي» .
Vol. 3, p. 143
1. (1). His statement "the leaders of the people of whims": if his intention is the Ahl al-Sunna, as is his habit in writing, of denouncing them, then he should be asked to point out the difference between them and the Muʿtazila, such that they deserve denunciation and the others do not. (ʿ)
2. . His statement "as if they had mixed it with their flesh": that is, they had blended it. (ʿ)
3. . Yā: for drawing attention, or for address, the one addressed being omitted. Al-maqfū: the one who is followed. Al-khuṭā: plural of khuṭwa (step), used figuratively for actions, on the basis of the shared sense of following in each; likewise "path" is used figuratively for the following, in respect of one's pursuing it and persevering in it. Mustawin: straight. Al-nahj, al-manhaj and al-minhāj: the clear road. Crookedness is used figuratively for obscuring and lying. ʿAjjū: they clamored and cried out.
1. (1) . قوله «رؤساء أهل الأهواء» إن كان مراده أهل السنة كما هو عادته في الكتابة من التشنيع عليهم، فينبغي مطالبته بالفرق بينهم وبين المعتزلة، حتى استحقوا التشنيع دونهم. (ع)
2. . قوله «وكأنهم ساطوه بلحومهم» أى خلطوه. (ع)
3. . يا: للتنبيه أو للنداء. والمنادى محذوف. والمقفو: المتبوع. والخطا: جمع خطوة، مستعارة للأفعال يجامع التبعية في كل، وكذلك الطريق مستعار للقفو من حيث اتباعه فيها ودوامه عليها. مستو: مستقيم. والنهج والمنهج والمنهاج: الطريق الواضح. والاعوجاج مستعار للبس وللكذب. وعجوا: ضجوا وصاحوا.
04
Q 22:3–4 · Vol. 3, pp. 143–144

Verses 3 to 4

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil." (3) "It has been decreed for him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will surely lead him astray and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze." (4)
وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطانٍ مَرِيدٍ (3) كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ مَنْ تَوَلاَّهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ وَيَهْدِيهِ إِلى عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ (4)
Vol. 3, p. 143
It is said: it was revealed regarding al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith, who was a contentious man who used to say: the angels are the daughters of God, the Qurʾān is the fables of the ancients, and God is not able to bring back to life one who has decayed and become dust. It is general, covering everyone who engages in disputation about what is permissible and impermissible to ascribe to God of attributes and acts, who does not rely on knowledge, does not bite into it with a firm molar, in whose dispute there is no following of proof and no submitting to fairness, so that he gropes like a she-camel with weak sight, unable to distinguish truth from falsehood. "And follows" in that, in his steps, "every devil" who is rebellious. It has become known of his condition, and is manifest and clear, that whoever takes him as an ally will gain nothing from his alliance except being led astray from the path to Paradise and being guided to the Fire. And I do not see the leaders of the people of whims (1), innovations and the Ḥashwiyya, who style themselves imams in God's religion, except as falling under all of this by first inclusion; indeed they are the most severe of devils in leading astray and the most effective in cutting off the road of truth, since they have set down error in writing and drilled their followers in it, as if they had mixed it with their flesh and blood (2). It is of them that the one who said had them in mind: "Many a one whose footsteps are followed among his people, whose path, in their eyes, to salvation is straight and clear; / Yet were they to read on the tablet what is inscribed there of the crookedness of his way, they would cry out (3)." O God, keep us firm upon the sound creed which You approved for Your angels in Your heavens and Your prophets on Your earth, and by Your mercy admit us among Your righteous servants. The decreeing (kitba) against him is a figure of speech, meaning: as though the leading astray of whoever takes him as ally were written against him and stamped upon him, because that is manifest in his condition. It has been read: annahu and fa-annahu, with fatḥa and with kasra. Whoever reads it with fatḥa does so because the first is the subject of "it has been decreed," and the second
قيل: نزلت في النضر بن الحرث، وكان جدلا يقول: الملائكة بنات الله، والقرآن أساطير الأولين، والله غير قادر على إحياء من بلى وصار ترابا. وهي عامة في كل من تعاطى الجدال فيما يجوز على الله وما لا يجوز من الصفات والأفعال، ولا يرجع إلى علم ولا يعضّ فيه بضرس قاطع، وليس فيه اتباع للبرهان ولا نزول على النصفة، فهو يخبط خبط عشواء، غير فارق بين الحق والباطل وَيَتَّبِعُ في ذلك خطوات كُلَّ شَيْطانٍ عات، علم من حاله وظهر وتبين أنه من جعله وليا له لم تثمر له ولايته إلا الإضلال عن طريق الجنة والهداية إلى النار. وما أرى رؤساء أهل الأهواء «1» والبدع والحشوية المتلقبين بالإمامة في دين الله إلا داخلين تحت كل هذا دخولا أوليا، بل هم أشدّ الشياطين إضلالا وأقطعهم لطريق الحق، حيث دوّنوا الضلال تدوينا ولقنوه أشياعهم تلقينا، وكأنهم ساطوه بلحومهم «2» ودمائهم، وإياهم عنى من قال: ويا ربّ مقفوّ الخطا بين قومه … طريق نجاة عندهم مستو نهج ولو قرءوا في الّلوح ما خطّ فيه من … بيان اعوجاج في طريقته عجّوا «3» اللهم ثبتنا على المعتقد الصحيح الذي رضيته لملائكتك في سمواتك، وأنبيائك في أرضك، وأدخلنا برحمتك في عبادك الصالحين. والكتبة عليه مثل، أى: كأنما كتب إضلال من يتولاه عليه ورقم به لظهور ذلك في حاله. وقرئ: أنه، فأنه بالفتح والكسر، فمن فتح فلأن الأول فاعل كتب، والثاني
Vol. 3, p. 144
is coordinated with it. Whoever reads it with kasra does so as a quotation of what was written, exactly as it is, as though (1) this statement had been written against him, as you say, "I wrote: Indeed God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy"; or on the assumption of an implied "it was said"; or on the ground that "it was decreed" contains the sense of speaking.
عطف عليه. ومن كسر فعلى حكاية المكتوب كما هو، كأنما «1» كتب عليه هذا الكلام، كما تقول: كتبت: إنّ الله هو الغنى الحميد. أو على تقدير: قيل. أو على أن كتب فيه معنى القول.

05
Q 22:5 · Vol. 3, pp. 144–145

Verse 5

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"O people, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, in order to make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whatever We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as infants, then [We nurture you] that you may reach your full strength. And among you is he who is taken in death, and among you is he who is returned to the most abject age, so that he knows, after having known, nothing. And you see the earth barren; then when We send down upon it water, it quivers and swells and grows every beautiful kind [of plant]." (5)
يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِنَ الْبَعْثِ فَإِنَّا خَلَقْناكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ مُضْغَةٍ مُخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي الْأَرْحامِ ما نَشاءُ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلاً ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوا أَشُدَّكُمْ وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُتَوَفَّى وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ إِلى أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ لِكَيْلا يَعْلَمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْئاً وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ هامِدَةً فَإِذا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهَا الْماءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ وَأَنْبَتَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ (5)
Vol. 3, p. 144
Al-Ḥasan read min al-baʿath with a fatḥa on the ʿayn; its parallel is al-jalab and al-ṭarad for al-jalb and al-ṭard. It is as though it were said: if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then what removes your doubt is that you consider the beginning of your creation. Al-ʿalaqa is a congealed piece of blood. Al-muḍgha is a small bit of flesh, about the size of what can be chewed. Al-mukhallaqa is that which has been made even and smooth, free of deficiency and defect. One says khalaqa al-siwāk wa-l-ʿūd when he has made it even and smoothed it, from their expression "a khalqāʾ rock," when it is smooth. It is as though God, Exalted is He, creates the lumps of flesh unequal: among them is that which is complete in form and smooth of defects, and among them that which is the opposite, and that inequality is followed by the inequality of people in their make and forms, in tallness and shortness, in completeness and deficiency. And We transferred you from state to state and from one formation to another only "to make clear to you," by this gradual process, our power and our wisdom, and that He who is able to create humankind first from dust, then secondly from a sperm-drop, though there is no kinship between water and dust, and who is able to make the sperm-drop a clot, though between them there is a manifest disparity, then to make the clot a lump of flesh and the lump of flesh bones, is able to restore what He began; indeed this is more within the scope of power than that, and easier by way of analogy. The verb's occurring without being made transitive to the thing made clear is an announcement that by these acts of His there becomes clear, of His power and knowledge, what no description can fathom and what no account can encompass. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read li-yubayyina lakum, and yuqirru with yāʾ. It has also been read wa-nuqirru, and nukhrijukum with nūn and the accusative; and yuqirru, yukhrijukum, and yuqirra, yukhrija, in the accusative and the nominative. From Yaʿqūb: nuqirru with nūn and ḍamma on the qāf, from qarra al-māʾ ("he poured the water"). The reading with the nominative is a statement that He settles in the wombs whatever We will to settle of that "for a specified term," which is the time of delivery, at the end of six months, or nine, or two years, or four, or whatever He wills and decrees. What He does not will to settle, the wombs expel or miscarry. The reading with the accusative is a causal clause coordinated to a causal clause.
قرأ الحسن مِنَ الْبَعْثِ بالتحريك. ونظيره: الجلب والطرد، في الجلب والطرد، كأنه قيل: إن ارتبتم في البعث فمزيل ريبكم أن تنظروا في بدء خلقكم. والعلقة: قطعة الدم الجامدة. والمضغة: اللحمة الصغيرة قدر ما يمضغ. والمخلقة: المسواة الملساء من النقصان والعيب. يقال: خلق السواك والعود، إذا سواه وملسه، من قولهم: صخرة خلقاء، وإذا كانت ملساة، كأنّ الله تعالى يخلق المضغ متفاوتة: منها ما هو كامل الخلقة أملس من العيوب، ومنها ما هو على عكس ذلك فيتبع ذلك التفاوت تفاوت الناس في خلقهم وصورهم وطولهم وقصرهم، وتمامهم ونقصانهم. وإنما نقلناكم من حال إلى حال ومن خلقة إلى خلقة لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بهذا التدريج قدرتنا وحكمتنا وأن من قدر على خلق البشر من تراب أولا، ثم من نطفة ثانيا ولا تناسب بين الماء والتراب وقدر على أن يجعل النطفة علقة وبينهما تباين ظاهر، ثم يجعل العلقة مضغة والمضغة عظاما: قدر على إعادة ما أبدأه، بل هذا أدخل في القدرة من تلك، وأهون في القياس. وورود الفعل غير معدى إلى المبين: إعلام بأن أفعاله هذه يتبين بها من قدرته وعلمه ما لا يكتنهه الذكر ولا يحيط به الوصف وقرأ ابن أبى عبلة: ليبين لكم. ويقرّ، بالياء. وقرئ: ونقرّ. ونخرجكم، بالنون والنصب. ويقرّ، ويخرجكم، ويقرّ، ويخرجكم: بالنصب والرفع. وعن يعقوب: نقرّ، بالنون وضم القاف، من قرّ الماء إذا صبه، فالقراءة بالرفع إخبار بأنه يقرّ فِي الْأَرْحامِ ما نَشاءُ أن يقرّه من ذلك إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى وهو وقت الوضع آخر ستة أشهر، أو تسعة، أو سنتين، أو أربع، أو كما شاء وقدّر. وما لم يشأ إقراره محته الأرحام أو أسقطته. والقراءة بالنصب: تعليل معطوف على تعليل.
Vol. 3, p. 145
Its meaning is: We created you by this gradual process for two purposes, one of which is that We make clear Our power, and the second that We settle in the wombs [whomever We settle] (from nuqirru), until they are born, grow up, and reach the limit of legal responsibility, so that I charge them. This reading is supported by His saying "then that you may reach your full strength," and by the singular "infant," since the purpose is to indicate the genus. It is also possible that the meaning is: We bring out each one of you as an infant. Al-ashudd is the perfection of strength, intellect and discernment, and it is one of the plural-form words for which no singular is used, like al-asidda (1), al-qutūd and al-abāṭīl and so on; it is as though it were a "strength" (shidda) in no single thing, and therefore built on a plural form. It has been read: wa-minkum man yutawaffā, that is, God takes him in death. "The most abject age" is senility and dotage, until he returns to his first condition in the time of his infancy: weak of frame, frivolous of mind, little of understanding. He made clear that just as He is able to raise him through degrees of increase until He brings him to the limit of completion, He is also able to bring him down until He ends with him at the lowest condition, "so that he knows, after having known, nothing," that is, so that he becomes forgetful to the point that if he acquires knowledge in something he does not long delay before forgetting it and the knowledge slips from him, so that he asks about it that very hour; he says to you: "Who is this?" and you say, "So-and-so," and he does not wait a moment before asking you about him again. Abū ʿAmr read al-ʿumr with a sukūn on the mīm. Al-hāmida is the dead, dried-up earth. This is a second proof of the Resurrection, and because of its obviousness and its being observed and seen, God repeated it in His Book. "It quivers and swells": it stirs with plant growth and puffs up. It has been read rabaʾat, meaning it rose. Al-bahīj is that which is beautiful, delighting him who looks at it.
ومعناه: خلقناكم مدرجين هذا التدريج لغرضين، أحدهما: أن نبين قدرتنا. والثاني: أن نقر في الأرحام من نقرّ، حتى يولدوا وينشؤا ويبلغوا حد التكليف فأكلفهم. ويعضد هذه القراءة قوله ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوا أَشُدَّكُمْ وحده لأن الغرض الدلالة على الجنس. ويحتمل: نخرج كل واحد منكم طفلا. الأشد: كمال القوة والعقل والتمييز، وهو من ألفاظ الجموع التي لم يستعمل لها واحد كالأسدّة «1» والقتود والأباطيل وغير ذلك، وكأنها شدّة في غير شيء واحد، فبنيت لذلك على لفظ الجمع. وقرئ: ومنكم من يتوفى، أى يتوفاه الله أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ الهرم والخرف، حتى يعود كهيئته الأولى في أوان طفولته: ضعيف البنية، سخيف العقل، قليل الفهم. بين أنه كما قدر على أن يرقيه في درجات الزيادة حتى يبلغه حد التمام، فهو قادر على أن يحطه حتى ينتهى به إلى الحالة السفلى لِكَيْلا يَعْلَمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْئاً أى: ليصير نساء بحيث إذا كسب علما في شيء لم ينشب أن ينساه ويزل عنه علمه حتى يسأل عنه من ساعته، يقول لك: من هذا؟ فتقول: فلان، فما يلبث لحظة إلا سألك عنه. وقرأ أبو عمرو: العمر، بسكون الميم. الهامدة: الميتة اليابسة. وهذه دلالة ثانية على البعث، ولظهورها وكونها مشاهدة معاينة، كررها الله في كتابه اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ تحرّكت بالنبات وانتفخت، وقرئ: ربأت، أى ارتفعت. البهيج: الحسن السارّ للناظر إليه.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 144
1. (1). His statement "huwa ka-annamā": perhaps it should be "ay ka-annamā." (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «هو كأنما» لعله: أى كأنما. (ع)
Vol. 3, p. 145
1. (1). His statement "one of the plural-form words for which no singular is used, like al-asidda, al-qutūd and al-abāṭīl": what is in al-Ṣiḥāḥ is: "al-sadd (with a fatḥa) is the singular of al-asidda, which are defects," end of quotation. It is like "blindness," "deafness" and "muteness," irregularly; by analogy its plural should have been sudūd. Al-qatad is the wood of the saddle, and its plural is qutūd and aqtād. Al-bāṭil is the opposite of the truth, and its plural abāṭīl is irregular, as though they had pluralized ibṭīl. In it also is God's saying "until he reaches his ashudd," meaning his strength, which is a singular that came in a plural pattern, like āank ("lead"), which is al-usrub, for neither of which is there a parallel. It is called a plural with no singular from its own wording, like abābīl, ʿabādīd and madhākīr. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «من ألفاظ الجموع التي لم يستعمل لها واحد كالأسدة والقتود والأباطيل» الذي في الصحاح «السدّ» بالفتح: واحد الأسدة وهي العيوب اه وهي مثل العمى والصمم والبكم على غير قياس، وكان قياسه: سدود. والقتد: خشب الرحل، وجمعه: قتود وأقتاد. والباطل: ضد الحق، والجمع أباطيل على غير قياس كأنهم جمعوا إبطيلا. وفيه أيضا قوله تعالى حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ أى قوته وهو واحد جاء على بناء الجمع، مثل «آنك» وهو الأسربّ، ولا نظير لهما، ويقال له: جمع لا واحد له من لفظه، مثل: أبابيل، وعباديد، ومذاكير. (ع)
06
Q 22:6–7 · Vol. 3, p. 145

Verses 6 to 7

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"That is because God is the Truth, and because He gives life to the dead, and because He is over all things competent," (6) "and because the Hour is coming, no doubt about it, and because God will resurrect those in the graves." (7)
ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّهُ يُحْيِ الْمَوْتى وَأَنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (6) وَأَنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ لا رَيْبَ فِيها وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ (7)
Vol. 3, p. 145
That is: that which we mentioned of the creation of the children of Adam and the revival of the earth, together with the kinds of wisdom and subtleties contained within that, comes about through this and this is the cause of its coming about, and without it its existence could not be conceived; and it is "because God is the Truth," that is, the established, the existent, and that He is able to give life to the dead and to everything within His power, and that He is wise and does not break His appointment, and He has promised the Hour and the Resurrection, so He must fulfill what He promised.
أى: ذلك الذي ذكرنا من خلق بنى آدم وإحياء الأرض، مع ما في تضاعيف ذلك من أصناف الحكم واللطائف، حاصل بهذا وهو السبب في حصوله، ولولاه لم يتصور كونه، وهو بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ أى الثابت الموجود، وأنه قادر على إحياء الموتى وعلى كل مقدور، وأنه حكيم لا يخلف ميعاده، وقد وعد الساعة والبعث، فلا بدّ أن يفي بما وعد.

07
Q 22:8–10 · Vol. 3, pp. 145–146

Verses 8 to 10

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening book," (8) "twisting his neck [in arrogance] to mislead [others] from the way of God. For him in this world is disgrace, and We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of burning." (9) "That is for what your hands have put forth and because God is not ever unjust to the servants." (10)
وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَلا هُدىً وَلا كِتابٍ مُنِيرٍ (8) ثانِيَ عِطْفِهِ لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَهُ فِي الدُّنْيا خِزْيٌ وَنُذِيقُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ (9) ذلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ يَداكَ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ (10)
Vol. 3, p. 146
It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he was Abū Jahl b. Hishām. It is also said: it is repeated just as the other stories are repeated. And it is said: the first concerns the imitators [of leaders], and this likewise concerns imitators. By "knowledge" is meant necessary knowledge; by "guidance," inference and rational inquiry, because it guides to cognition; and by "an enlightening book," revelation. That is: he disputes on the basis of conjecture and guesswork, not by any of these three. "Twisting the neck" is an expression for pride and conceit, like turning the cheek away and bending the neck. It is also said to mean turning away from the Reminder. From al-Ḥasan: thāniya ʿaṭfihi, with a fatḥa on the ʿayn, that is, one who withholds his tenderness. "To mislead" is a causal clause for the disputation. It has been read with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and with a fatḥa.
عن ابن عباس أنه أبو جهل بن هشام. وقيل: كرر كما كررت سائر الأقاصيص. وقيل: الأوّل في المقلدين، وهذا في المقلدين. والمراد بالعلم: العلم الضروري. وبالهدى: الاستدلال والنظر، لأنه يهدى إلى المعرفة. وبالكتاب المنير: الوحى، أى يجادل بظن وتخمين، لا بأحد هذه الثلاثة. وثنى العطف: عبارة عن الكبر والخيلاء، كتصعير الخدّ ولىّ الجيد. وقيل: عن الإعراض عن الذكر. وعن الحسن: ثانى عطفه، بفتح العين، أى: مانع تعطفه لِيُضِلَّ تعليل للمجادلة. قرئ بضم الياء وفتحها.
Question
If you ask: what was his aim in his disputing, to lead astray "from the way of God"? So how is it given as the cause? And he was not guided in the first place, so that by disputing he would leave guidance for error.
فإن قلت: ما كان غرضه من جداله الضلال عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فكيف علل به؟ وما كان أيضا مهتديا حتى إذا جادل خرج بالجدال من الهدى إلى الضلال؟
Answer
I say: since his disputation ended in leading astray, it was made as though that were his aim; and since guidance was presented to him, and he left it and turned away from it and took up disputing with falsehood, he was made like one leaving guidance for error. His "disgrace" is what befell him at Badr of humiliation and killing; and the cause of what he has been afflicted with of the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the next is "what his hands have put forth," and God's justice in punishing the wicked and rewarding the righteous.
قلت: لما أدّى جداله إلى الضلال، جعل كأنه غرضه، ولما كان الهدى معرضا له فتركه وأعرض عنه وأقبل على الجدال بالباطل، جعل كالخارج من الهدى إلى الضلال. وخزيه: ما أصابه يوم بدر من الصغار والقتل، والسبب فيما منى به من خزى الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة: هو ما قدمت يداه، وعدل الله في معاقبته الفجار وإثابته الصالحين.

1. (1). Thus al-Wāḥidī mentions it in al-Asbāb, but without a chain, saying: ʿAṭiyya reported from Abū Saʿīd, and then mentioned it. Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted it from the transmission of ʿAṭiyya from Abū Saʿīd, who said: "A man of the Jews became Muslim and his wealth and children were lost, and he took Islam as an ill omen," the ḥadīth being similar. Its chain is weak. Al-ʿUqaylī transmitted it from the transmission of ʿAnbasa b. Saʿīd from Abū al-Zubayr from Jābir, who said: "A Jew came to the Prophet ﷺ and became Muslim at his hands, then returned to his home and was afflicted in his eye and in his children, and returned to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'Release me,'" the ḥadīth; and it does not mention in it the revelation of the verse. And ʿAnbasa is very weak.
1. (1) . هكذا ذكره الواحدي في الأسباب، لكن بغير إسناد. فقال: روى عطية عن أبى سعيد، فذكره سواه وأخرجه ابن مردويه من رواية عطية عن أبى سعيد قال «أسلم رجل من اليهود فذهب ماله وولده، وتشاءم بالإسلام- الحديث نحوه» وإسناده ضعيف وأخرج العقيلي من رواية عنبسة بن سعيد عن أبى الزبير عن جابر قال: «أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يهودى فأسلم على يديه، ثم رجع إلى منزله فأصيب في عينه وفي ولده فرجع إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. فقال: أقلنى- الحديث» ولم يذكر فيه نزول الآية. وعنبسة ضعيف جدا.
08
Q 22:11–13 · Vol. 3, pp. 146–147

Verses 11 to 13

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And among the people is he who worships God on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it; but if he is struck by trial, he turns on his face [in apostasy]. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss." (11) "He invokes, other than God, that which neither harms him nor benefits him. That is the extreme error." (12) "He invokes one whose harm is nearer than his benefit. How wretched the protector and how wretched the companion!" (13)
وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ عَلى حَرْفٍ فَإِنْ أَصابَهُ خَيْرٌ اطْمَأَنَّ بِهِ وَإِنْ أَصابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ انْقَلَبَ عَلى وَجْهِهِ خَسِرَ الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةَ ذلِكَ هُوَ الْخُسْرانُ الْمُبِينُ (11) يَدْعُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَضُرُّهُ وَما لا يَنْفَعُهُ ذلِكَ هُوَ الضَّلالُ الْبَعِيدُ (12) يَدْعُوا لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ لَبِئْسَ الْمَوْلى وَلَبِئْسَ الْعَشِيرُ (13)
Vol. 3, p. 146
"On an edge" means on a border of religion, not in its middle and heart. This is a parable for their being in unrest and agitation in their religion, not in calm and reassurance, like one who is on the edge of an army: if he senses victory and spoils he stays and is at ease, and otherwise he flees and bolts headlong. They said: it was revealed regarding Bedouins who came to Medina; when one of them was healthy in body, his mare foaled a noble colt, his wife bore a sound boy, and his wealth and livestock multiplied, he would say: "I have met with nothing but good since I entered this religion of mine," and was reassured. And if matters were otherwise he would say: "I have met with nothing but evil," and turned back. It is reported from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that a man of the Jews became Muslim and then misfortunes struck him, and he took Islam as an ill omen. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Release me [from my pledge]," and he said: "Islam is not given up" (1), and so the verse was revealed. The one stricken by trial, by abandoning submission to God's decree and going out to that which angers God:
عَلى حَرْفٍ على طرف من الدين لا في وسطه وقلبه. وهذا مثل لكونهم على قلق واضطراب في دينهم، لا على سكون وطمأنينة، كالذي يكون على طرف من العسكر، فإن أحسّ بظفر وغنيمه قرّ واطمأن، وإلا فرّ وطار على وجهه. قالوا: نزلت في أعاريب قدموا المدينة، وكان أحدهم إذا صح بدنه ونتجت فرسه مهرا سريا، وولدت امرأته غلاما سويا، وكثر ماله وماشيته قال: ما أصبت منذ دخلت في دينى هذا إلا خيرا، واطمأن. وإن كان الأمر بخلافه قال: ما أصبت إلا شرا، وانقلب. وعن أبى سعيد الخدري أن رجلا من اليهود أسلم فأصابته مصائب، فتشاءم بالإسلام، فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أقلنى، فقال «إنّ الإسلام لا يقال» «1» فنزلت. المصاب بالمحنة بترك التسليم لقضاء الله والخروج إلى ما يسخط الله:
Vol. 3, p. 147
brings together upon himself two trials, one of which is the loss of what he was afflicted with, and the second the loss of the reward of the patient; so it is the loss of both abodes. It has been read: khāsiru al-dunyā wa-l-ākhira, in the accusative and in the nominative; the accusative is as a circumstantial qualifier, and the nominative as agent. The use of the explicit noun in place of the pronoun is a fine device; or it is read as the predicate of an omitted subject. "The extreme error" is borrowed from the error of one who goes far astray into the wilderness, so that the distance of his error grows long and remote.
جامع على نفسه محنتين، إحداهما: ذهاب ما أصيب به. والثانية: ذهاب ثواب الصابرين، فهو خسران الدارين. وقرئ: خاسر الدنيا والآخرة بالنصب والرفع، فالنصب على الحال، والرفع على الفاعلية. ووضع الظاهر موضع الضمير، وهو وجه حسن. أو على أنه خبر مبتدإ محذوف. استعير الضَّلالُ الْبَعِيدُ من ضلال من أبعد في التيه ضالا، فطالت وبعدت مسافة ضلالته.
Question
If you ask: harm and benefit are denied of the idols in one verse and affirmed of them in the two verses [that follow], and this is a contradiction.
فإن قلت: الضرر والنفع منفيان عن الأصنام مثبتان لها في الآيتين، وهذا تناقض.
Answer
I say: once the meaning is grasped, this fancy disappears. It is that God, Exalted is He, declared the unbeliever foolish for worshipping an inanimate thing that has no power over harm or benefit, while he, in his ignorance and error, believes that he will benefit from it when he seeks its intercession; then He says: on the Day of Resurrection this unbeliever will say, with cries and shrieks, when he sees that he has been harmed by the idols and has entered the Fire through worshipping them, and sees no trace of the intercession he claimed for them: "[He invokes] one whose harm is nearer than his benefit. How wretched the protector and how wretched the companion!" Or else "he invokes" is repeated, as if He had said: he invokes, he invokes, besides God, that which neither harms him nor benefits him; then said: [he invokes] one whose harm, through his being worshipped, is nearer than his benefit, through his being an intercessor: how wretched the protector! In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [b. Masʿūd]: man ḍarruhu, without the lām. Al-mawlā is the helper, and al-ʿashīr is the companion, as in His saying, "and wretched is the companion."
قلت: إذا حصل المعنى ذهب هذا الوهم، وذلك أن الله تعالى سفه الكافر بأنه يعبد جمادا لا يملك ضرا ولا نفعا، وهو يعتقد فيه بجهله وضلاله أنه يستنفع به حين يستشفع به، ثم قال: يوم القيامة يقول هذا الكافر بدعاء وصراخ، حين يرى استضراره بالأصنام ودخوله النار بعبادتها، ولا يرى أثر الشفاعة التي ادعاها لها لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ لَبِئْسَ الْمَوْلى وَلَبِئْسَ الْعَشِيرُ أو كرّر يدعو، كأنه قال: يدعو يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه، ثم قال: لمن ضره بكونه معبودا أقرب من نفعه بكونه شفيعا لبئس المولى. وفي حرف عبد الله: من ضره، بغير لام. المولى: الناصر. والعشير: الصاحب، كقوله فَبِئْسَ الْقَرِينُ.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 146
1. (1). Thus al-Wāḥidī mentions it in al-Asbāb, but without a chain, saying: ʿAṭiyya reported from Abū Saʿīd, and then mentioned it. Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted it from the transmission of ʿAṭiyya from Abū Saʿīd, who said: "A man of the Jews became Muslim and his wealth and children were lost, and he took Islam as an ill omen," the ḥadīth being similar. Its chain is weak. Al-ʿUqaylī transmitted it from the transmission of ʿAnbasa b. Saʿīd from Abū al-Zubayr from Jābir, who said: "A Jew came to the Prophet ﷺ and became Muslim at his hands, then returned to his home and was afflicted in his eye and in his children, and returned to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'Release me,'" the ḥadīth; and it does not mention in it the revelation of the verse. And ʿAnbasa is very weak.
1. (1) . هكذا ذكره الواحدي في الأسباب، لكن بغير إسناد. فقال: روى عطية عن أبى سعيد، فذكره سواه وأخرجه ابن مردويه من رواية عطية عن أبى سعيد قال «أسلم رجل من اليهود فذهب ماله وولده، وتشاءم بالإسلام- الحديث نحوه» وإسناده ضعيف وأخرج العقيلي من رواية عنبسة بن سعيد عن أبى الزبير عن جابر قال: «أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يهودى فأسلم على يديه، ثم رجع إلى منزله فأصيب في عينه وفي ولده فرجع إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. فقال: أقلنى- الحديث» ولم يذكر فيه نزول الآية. وعنبسة ضعيف جدا.

09
Q 22:14–15 · Vol. 3, pp. 147–148

Verses 14 to 15

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, God does what He intends." (14) "Whoever should think that God will not support him [the Prophet] in this world and the Hereafter, let him extend a rope to the ceiling [of his house], then cut off [his breath], and let him see whether his scheme will remove that which enrages [him]." (15)
إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ ما يُرِيدُ (14) مَنْ كانَ يَظُنُّ أَنْ لَنْ يَنْصُرَهُ اللَّهُ فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إِلَى السَّماءِ ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ فَلْيَنْظُرْ هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ ما يَغِيظُ (15)
Vol. 3, p. 147
This is speech into which abridgment has entered. The meaning is: God is the supporter of His Messenger in this world and the next; so whoever of his enviers and enemies thinks that God will do otherwise, and hopes for that, and is enraged that he will attain what he seeks, let him exhaust his capacity and expend his whole effort in removing what enrages him, by doing what is done by one whose rage has reached its utmost, until he stretches a rope to the roof of his house and hangs himself; then let him look, and picture to himself, whether, if he does that, it will take away the support of God that enrages him. He called hanging "cutting" because one who hangs himself cuts off his own breath by blocking its passages; from this one calls shortness of breath "cutting" (1). He called his act "a scheme" because he put it in the place of scheming, since he was unable to do
هذا كلام قد دخله اختصار. والمعنى. إن الله ناصر رسوله في الدنيا والاخرة، فمن كان يظنّ من حاسديه وأعاديه أن الله يفعل خلاف ذلك ويطمع فيه، ويغيظه أنه يظفر بمطلوبه، فليستقص وسعه وليستفرغ مجهوده في إزالة ما يغيظه، بأن يفعل ما يفعل من بلغ منه الغيظ كل مبلغ حتى مدّ حبلا إلى سماء بيته فاختنق، فلينظر وليصوّر في نفسه أنه إن فعل ذلك هل يذهب نصر الله الذي يغيظه؟ وسمى الاختناق قطعا لأنّ المختنق يقطع نفسه بحبس مجاريه. ومنه قيل للبهر: القطع «1» . وسمى فعله كيدا لأنه وضعه موضع الكيد، حيث لم يقدر على
Vol. 3, p. 148
anything else; or by way of mockery, because the one he envies was not schemed against by him, he only schemed against himself. The meaning is: he has in his hand nothing but what will not remove that which enrages him. It is also said: let him extend a rope to the overshadowing sky, and let him climb upon it and cut off the revelation, or [cut off] what is sent down upon him [the Prophet]. And it is said: some of the Muslims, from the intensity of their rage and anger against the polytheists, found slow the victory that God had promised His Messenger, while others of the polytheists wished to follow him and feared that his affair would not stand firm. So this was revealed. "Support" has also been interpreted as provision; and it is said that the meaning is that provisions are in God's hand and are not obtained except by His will, and the servant must be content with his allotment; so whoever thinks that God will not provide for him, and has no patience and submission, let him reach the utmost limit of impatience, which is hanging himself, for that will not change the allotment nor make him provided for.
غيره. أو على سبيل الاستهزاء لأنه لم يكد به محسوده إنما كاد به نفسه. والمراد: ليس في يده إلا ما ليس بمذهب لما يغيظه. وقيل: فليمدد بحبل إلى السماء المظلة. وليصعد عليه فليقطع الوحى أو ينزل عليه. وقيل: كان قوم من المسلمين لشدّة غيظهم وحنقهم على المشركين يستبطئون ما وعد الله رسوله من النصر، وآخرون من المشركين يريدون اتباعه ويخشون أن لا يثبت أمره. فنزلت. وقد فسر النصر: بالرزق، وقيل: معناه أن الأرزاق بيد الله لا تنال إلا بمشيئته ولا بد للعبد من الرضا بقسمته، فمن ظنّ أن الله غير رازقه وليس به صبر واستسلام، فليبلغ غاية الجزع وهو الاختناق، فإن ذلك لا يقلب القسمة ولا يردّه مرزوقا.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 147
1. (1). His statement "from this one calls shortness of breath 'cutting'": that is, the succession of breaths. Al-Ṣiḥāḥ gives this. (ʿ)

Sarbalahu: He clothed him with kingship resembling a robe (sirbāl). It is also related: "sirbāla mulkin bihi," that is, with that garment or kingship, tuzjā: driven. Al-khawātīm: plural of khātam (with fatḥa and kasra); the original is khawātim, and the yāʾ was added. What is meant by it is the outcomes of praiseworthy affairs. Abū Ḥayyān said: it is possible that the predicate of inna is "bihi tuzjā," and the sentence "inna Allāh sarbalahu" is parenthetical. It is also related as "bihi turjā" with rāʾ; this should be verified.
1. (1) . لجرير. وقوله «إن الله سربله» خير إن الأولى، وكررها لتوكيد التوكيد. وسربله: كساه بالملك الشبيه بالسربال. ويروى: سربال ملك به، أى: بذلك اللباس أو الملك، تزجى: أى تساق الخواتيم: جمع خاتم- بالفتح والكسر- والأصل: خواتم، فزيدت الياء. والمراد بها: عواقب الأمور الحميدة. وقال أبو حيان: يحتمل أن خبر إن قوله «به تزجى» وجملة «إن الله سربله» اعتراضية. ويروى: «به ترجى» بالراء، وليحرر.

Q 22:16 · Vol. 3, p. 148

Verse 16

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And thus We have sent it down as clear verses, and because God guides whom He intends." (16)
وَكَذلِكَ أَنْزَلْناهُ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يُرِيدُ (16)
Vol. 3, p. 148
That is: just as that sending down, We have sent down the Qurʾān in its entirety as clear verses, and [We sent it down] so that God may guide by it those whom He knows will believe; or He strengthens those who believe and increases them in guidance; He sent it down in this way, making clear.
أى: ومثل ذلك الإنزال أنزلنا القرآن كله آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ وَل أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي به الذين يعلم أنهم يؤمنون. أو يثبت الذين آمنوا ويزيدهم هدى، أنزله كذلك مبينا

Q 22:17 · Vol. 3, p. 148

Verse 17

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"Indeed, those who have believed, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associate others with God: God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God is over all things a Witness." (17)
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هادُوا وَالصَّابِئِينَ وَالنَّصارى وَالْمَجُوسَ وَالَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ (17)
Vol. 3, p. 148
"Judging" (faṣl) is unrestricted, and may include separating them in all conditions and places, so that He does not recompense them with one recompense without distinction, nor gather them in one place. It is said: the religions are five: four belong to Satan and one to the Merciful. The Sabians were placed with the Christians because they are a type among them. It is also said that "He will judge between them" means He will decide between them, that is, between the believers and the unbelievers. Inna was introduced upon each of the two parts of the sentence to increase the emphasis. Similar is the saying of Jarīr: "Indeed the Caliph, indeed God has clothed him with a robe of kingship, by which the outcomes are driven (1)."
الفصل مطلق يحتمل الفصل بينهم في الأحوال والأماكن جميعا، فلا يجازيهم جزاء واحدا بغير تفاوت، ولا يجمعهم في موطن واحد. وقيل: الأديان خمسة: أربعة للشيطان وواحد للرحمن. جعل الصابئون مع النصارى لأنهم نوع منهم. وقيل يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يقضى بينهم، أى بين المؤمنين والكافرين. وأدخلت إِنَّ على كل واحد من جزأى الجملة لزيادة التوكيد. ونحوه قول جرير: إنّ الخليفة إنّ الله سربله … سربال ملك به ترجى الخواتيم «1»

Q 22:18 · Vol. 3, pp. 148–149

Verse 18

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"Do you not see that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures, and many of the people? But many have deserved the punishment. And whoever God humiliates, for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, God does what He wills." (18)
أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ وَالنُّجُومُ وَالْجِبالُ وَالشَّجَرُ وَالدَّوَابُّ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذابُ وَمَنْ يُهِنِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ مُكْرِمٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ ما يَشاءُ (18)
Vol. 3, p. 149
their obedience to Him, in respect of what He brings about in them of His acts and what He makes proceed upon them of His management and subjection of them, is called prostration to Him, likening their obedience to bringing the acts of the one who is charged with duties into the category of obedience and submission, which is the prostration beneath which every other humility falls.
سميت مطاوعتها له فيما يحدث فيها من أفعاله ويجريها عليه من تدبيره وتسخيره لها: سجودا له، تشبيها لمطاوعتها بإدخال أفعال المكلف في باب الطاعة والانقياد، وهو السجود الذي كل خضوع دونه،
Question
If you ask: what will you do with His saying "and many of the people," and the two objections it contains? The first is that prostration in the sense you have interpreted it is not performed by some people and not by others. The second is that prostration was first ascribed in general to those on the earth, of humankind and jinn, so that ascribing it afterwards to many of them is a contradiction?
فإن قلت: فما تصنع بقوله وَكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ وبما فيه من الاعتراضين، أحدهما: أنّ السجود على المعنى الذي فسرته به، لا يسجده بعض الناس دون بعض. والثاني: أنّ السجود قد أسند على سبيل العموم إلى من في الأرض من الإنس والجن أولا، فإسناده إلى كثير منهم آخرا مناقضة؟
Answer
I say: I do not connect "many" with the individual items arranged in series and falling under the verb's governance; rather I make it nominative by an implied verb that His saying "prostrates" indicates, that is: and many of the people prostrate to Him with the prostration of obedience and worship. I do not say that I interpret "prostrates," which is explicit, in the sense of obedience and worship in the case of these, because a single expression cannot properly be used in a single state in two different meanings. Or I make it nominative as a subject whose predicate is omitted, namely "rewarded," since the predicate of its counterpart indicates it, which is His saying "have deserved the punishment." It is also permissible to make "of the people" its predicate, that is: of the people who are people in truth, namely the righteous and the God-fearing. And it is permissible to exaggerate the multiplicity of those who deserve punishment by coordinating "many" with "many," then reporting of them that "the punishment has been deserved by them," as though it were said: "and many and many of the people, the punishment is due upon them." It has been read: ḥuqqa with a ḍamma; and it has been read: ḥaqqan, meaning: the punishment is truly due upon them. And whomever God has humiliated (by decreeing wretchedness against him because of what preceded in His knowledge of his unbelief or sinfulness) remains humiliated (1); you will find for him no one to honor him. It has been read mukram with a fatḥa on the rāʾ in the sense of ikrām. "Indeed, He does what He wills" of honoring and humiliating, and He wills of that only what the deeds of the doers and the beliefs of the believers require.
قلت: لا أنظم كثيرا في المفردات المتناسقة الداخلة تحت حكم الفعل، وإنما أرفعه بفعل مضمر يدل عليه قوله يَسْجُدُ أى ويسجد له كثير من الناس سجود طاعة وعبادة. ولم أقل: أفسر يسجد الذي هو ظاهر بمعنى الطاعة والعبادة في حق هؤلاء، لأنّ اللفظ الواحد لا يصحّ استعماله في حالة واحدة على معنيين مختلفين، أو أرفعه على الابتداء والخبر محذوف وهو مثاب، لأنّ خبر مقابله يدل عليه، وهو قوله حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذابُ ويجوز أن يجعل مِنَ النَّاسِ خبرا له، أى: من الناس الذين هم الناس على الحقيقة وهم الصالحون والمتقون. ويجوز أن يبالغ في تكثير المحقوقين بالعذاب، فيعطف كثير على كثير، ثم يخبر عنهم بحقّ عليهم العذاب، كأنه قيل: وكثير وكثير من الناس حق عليهم العذاب، وقرئ: حق، بالضم. وقرئ: حقا، أى حقّ عليهم العذاب حقا. ومن أهانه الله- بأن كتب عليه الشقاوة لما سبق في علمه من كفره أو فسقه- فقد بقي مهانا «1» ، لن تجد له مكرما. وقرئ: مكرم، بفتح الراء بمعنى الإكرام. إنه يَفْعَلُ ما يَشاءُ من الإكرام والإهانة، ولا يشاء من ذلك إلا ما يقتضيه عمل العاملين واعتقاد المعتقدين.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 148
1. (1). By Jarīr. His saying "inna Allāh sarbalahu" is the predicate of the first inna, and he repeated it for the emphasis of the emphasis. Sarbalahu: He clothed him with kingship resembling a robe (sirbāl). It is also related: "sirbāla mulkin bihi," that is, with that garment or kingship, tuzjā: driven. Al-khawātīm: plural of khātam (with fatḥa and kasra); the original is khawātim, and the yāʾ was added. What is meant by it is the outcomes of praiseworthy affairs. Abū Ḥayyān said: it is possible that the predicate of inna is "bihi tuzjā," and the sentence "inna Allāh sarbalahu" is parenthetical. It is also related as "bihi turjā" with rāʾ; this should be verified.
1. (1) . لجرير. وقوله «إن الله سربله» خير إن الأولى، وكررها لتوكيد التوكيد. وسربله: كساه بالملك الشبيه بالسربال. ويروى: سربال ملك به، أى: بذلك اللباس أو الملك، تزجى: أى تساق الخواتيم: جمع خاتم- بالفتح والكسر- والأصل: خواتم، فزيدت الياء. والمراد بها: عواقب الأمور الحميدة. وقال أبو حيان: يحتمل أن خبر إن قوله «به تزجى» وجملة «إن الله سربله» اعتراضية. ويروى: «به ترجى» بالراء، وليحرر.
Vol. 3, p. 149
1. (1). His statement "because of his unbelief or sinfulness he remains humiliated" is built on the view that the sinner is an intermediate between the believer and the unbeliever, and that he abides eternally in the Fire like the unbeliever, which is the school of the Muʿtazila. The truth, according to the Ahl al-Sunna, is that he is a believer, and if he enters the Fire he is brought out of it by intercession or by God's grace alone. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «من كفره أو فسقه فقد بقي مهانا» مبنى على أن الفاسق واسطة بين المؤمن والكافر، وأنه يخلد في النار كالكافر، وهو مذهب المعتزلة. والحق عند أهل السنة أنه مؤمن، وإن دخل النار مخرج منها بالشفاعة أو بمجرد فضله تعالى. (ع)

Q 22:19–22 · Vol. 3, pp. 149–150

Verses 19 to 22

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"These are two adversaries who have disputed concerning their Lord. But those who disbelieved will have cut out for them garments of fire; poured over their heads will be scalding water," (19) "by which is melted that within their bellies and [their] skins." (20) "And for them are maces of iron." (21) "Every time they wish to get out of it, from anguish, they will be returned to it, and [it will be said], 'Taste the punishment of the Burning.'" (22)
هذانِ خَصْمانِ اخْتَصَمُوا فِي رَبِّهِمْ فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيابٌ مِنْ نارٍ يُصَبُّ مِنْ فَوْقِ رُؤُسِهِمُ الْحَمِيمُ (19) يُصْهَرُ بِهِ ما فِي بُطُونِهِمْ وَالْجُلُودُ (20) وَلَهُمْ مَقامِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ (21) كُلَّما أَرادُوا أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْها مِنْ غَمٍّ أُعِيدُوا فِيها وَذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ (22)
Vol. 3, p. 149
Al-khaṣm is an attribute used to describe a troop or party, as though it were said: "these are two troops, or two parties, in dispute." His saying "these two" is in accordance with the wording, and "they disputed" in accordance with the meaning, as in His saying "and among them are those who listen to you until, when they leave"
الخصم: صفة وصف بها الفوج أو الفريق، فكأنه قيل: هذان فوجان أو فريقان مختصمان وقوله هذانِ للفظ. واخْتَصَمُوا للمعنى، كقوله وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ حَتَّى إِذا خَرَجُوا
Vol. 3, p. 150
[from the verse] ...had it been said "these are two adversaries" (khaṣmān) or "they disputed," it would have been permissible. What is meant are the believers and the unbelievers. Ibn ʿAbbās said: it refers back to the people of the six religions. "Concerning their Lord" means concerning His religion and attributes. It is reported that the People of the Book said to the believers: "We have a greater claim to God, and our Book is older than yours, and our prophet is before your prophet." The believers said: "We have a greater claim to God: we believed in Muḥammad, and we believed in your prophet and in whatever Book God has sent down, while you know our Book and our prophet, then you abandoned him and disbelieved in him out of envy." This is their dispute concerning their Lord. "But those who disbelieved..." is the decision of the dispute meant by His saying, Exalted is He, "God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection." In a report from al-Kisāʾī: khiṣmān, with a kasra. It has been read qutṭiʿat in the lightened form, as though God, Exalted is He, will measure out for them fires according to the measure of their bodies, enveloping them as worn garments are cut to measure. It is also possible that those fires will be layered upon each of them, like garments layered upon the wearer, one over another. Similar is "their garments will be of pitch." Al-ḥamīm is hot water. From Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ: "If a drop of it fell upon the mountains of the world it would melt them." "Is melted" (yuṣharu) means dissolved. From al-Ḥasan, with a doubled hāʾ for intensification: that is, when the scalding water is poured over their heads, its effect upon the inside is like its effect upon the outside, so that it dissolves their entrails and intestines just as it dissolves their skins; this is more forceful than His saying "and they will be given scalding water to drink, and it will cut their intestines to pieces." Al-maqāmiʿ are whips. In the ḥadīth: "If one of its maces were placed upon the earth and the two weighty creatures [humans and jinn] gathered upon it, they could not lift it (1)." Al-Aʿmash read ruddū fīhā. Restoring and returning can occur only after exit, so the meaning is: every time they wish to get out of it from anguish and do get out, they are returned into it. The meaning of the exiting is what is reported from al-Ḥasan: that the Fire strikes them with its flame and lifts them, until, when they are at its highest, they are struck with the maces and fall back into it for seventy autumns; and "it will be said to them: Taste the punishment of the Burning." Al-ḥarīq is the dense fire, spread widely, utterly destructive.
ولو قيل: هؤلاء خصمان. أو اختصما: جاز. يراد المؤمنون والكافرون. قال ابن عباس: رجع إلى أهل الأديان الستة فِي رَبِّهِمْ أى في دينه وصفاته. وروى أن أهل الكتاب قالوا للمؤمنين: نحن أحق بالله، وأقدم منكم كتابا، ونبينا قبل نبيكم. وقال المؤمنون: نحن أحق بالله، آمنا بمحمد، وآمنا بنبيكم وبما أنزل الله من كتاب، وأنتم تعرفون كتابنا ونبينا ثم تركتموه وكفرتم به حسدا، فهذه خصومتهم في ربهم فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هو فصل الخصومة المعنىّ بقوله تعالى إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وفي رواية عن الكسائي: خصمان، بالكسر، وقرئ: قطعت بالتخفيف، كأنّ الله تعالى يقدّر لهم نيرانا على مقادير جثثهم تشتمل عليهم كما تقطع الثياب الملبوسة. ويجوز أن تظاهر على كل واحد منهم تلك النيران كالثياب المظاهرة على اللابس بعضها فوق بعض. ونحوه سَرابِيلُهُمْ مِنْ قَطِرانٍ. الْحَمِيمُ الماء الحار. عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنه: لو سقطت منه نقطة على جبال الدنيا لأذابتها يُصْهَرُ يذاب. وعن الحسن بتشديد الهاء للمبالغة، أى: إذا صبّ الحميم على رؤسهم كان تأثيره في الباطن نحو تأثيره في الظاهر، فيذيب أحشاءهم وأمعاءهم كما يذيب جلودهم، وهو أبلغ من قوله وَسُقُوا ماءً حَمِيماً فَقَطَّعَ أَمْعاءَهُمْ والمقامع: السياط. في الحديث: «لو وضعت مقمعة منها في الأرض فاجتمع عليها الثقلان ما أقلوها «1» » ، وقرأ الأعمش: ردوا فيها. والإعادة والرد لا يكون إلا بعد الخروج، فالمعنى: كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها من غم فخرجوا أعيدوا فيها. ومعنى الخروج: ما يروى عن الحسن أنّ النار تضربهم بلهبها فترفعهم، حتى إذا كانوا في أعلاها ضربوا بالمقامع فهووا فيها سبعين خريفا وَقيل لهم ذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ والحريق: الغليظ من النار المنتشر العظيم الإهلاك.

Q 22:23–25 · Vol. 3, pp. 150–152

Verses 23 to 25

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk." (23) "And they were guided to the purest of speech, and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy." (24) "Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God and from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, which We made for the people, equal are the resident therein and the visitor, and whoever intends therein [a deed of] deviation [in the form of] wrongdoing: We will make him taste of a painful punishment." (25)
إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِنْ أَساوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَلُؤْلُؤاً وَلِباسُهُمْ فِيها حَرِيرٌ (23) وَهُدُوا إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَهُدُوا إِلى صِراطِ الْحَمِيدِ (24) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَالْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ الَّذِي جَعَلْناهُ لِلنَّاسِ سَواءً الْعاكِفُ فِيهِ وَالْبادِ وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ (25)
Vol. 3, p. 150
"They will be adorned": from Ibn ʿAbbās: from "the woman was adorned (ḥuliyat), so she is adorned (ḥālin)" (2). "And pearls" in the accusative, on the sense of
يُحَلَّوْنَ عن ابن عباس: من حليت المرأة فهي حال «2» وَلُؤْلُؤاً بالنصب على:
Vol. 3, p. 151
"and they will be given pearls," as in "and fair ones with wide lovely eyes." [The qirāʾāt:] lūlūan with the second hamza turned into wāw; lūliyan, with both turned into wāws, then the second turned into yāʾ, like adlin; lūlin, like adlin, for those who read it in the genitive; lūlūʾin; and līliyan, with both turned into yāʾs. From Ibn ʿAbbās: "they were guided": God guided them and inspired them to say: "Praise be to God, who has been true to us in His promise," and guided them to the path of Paradise. One says: "So-and-so does good to the poor and raises up the oppressed," without meaning present or future, but meaning the continual existence of the doing of good from him and of the raising up throughout all his times and moments. From this is His saying, Exalted is He, "and they avert [people] from the way of God," that is, the averting from them is continuous and perpetual. "For the people" means those to whom the name "people" applies, without distinction between resident and bedouin, between long-settled dweller and newcomer, between Meccan and one from the outlying regions. The companions of Abū Ḥanīfa cited this as evidence, saying that what is meant by al-Masjid al-Ḥarām is Mecca, on the ground that it is not permissible to sell the houses of Mecca or to lease them. According to al-Shāfiʿī, that is not prohibited. Isḥāq b. Rāhawayh debated this and argued with His saying "those who were expelled from their homes," and said: does He ascribe the homes to their owners, or to others? And did ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may God Exalted be pleased with him, buy the house of the prison from its owners or from others? "Equal" (sawāʾan) in the accusative is Ḥafṣ's reading; the others read it in the nominative. The reason for the accusative is that it is the second object of "We made it," that is, "We made it equal, the resident therein and the visitor." In the reading with the nominative, the [nominal] sentence is the second object. Al-ilḥād is deviation from the straight course, and originally it is the "deviation" of a hoof [from the track]. His sayings "of deviation" and "of wrongdoing" are two synonymous circumstantial qualifiers. The object of "intends" is left unspecified so as to include everything that may be included, as if He said: whoever intends therein any intention, deviating from the straight course, wrongfully, "We will make him taste of a painful punishment," meaning that the obligation upon one who is in it is to restrain himself and follow the path of rectitude and justice in everything he aims at and intends. It is also said: ilḥād in the Sanctuary is preventing people from building it up; and from Saʿīd b. Jubayr: hoarding for profit. From ʿAṭāʾ: a man's saying in a sale, "No, by God" and "Yes, by God." From ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr [it is related] that he had two tents, one in the unconsecrated area and the other in the Sanctuary, and when he wished to reproach his family he would reproach them in the unconsecrated area (2). When he was asked about it, he said: "We used to be told that part of ilḥād in it is a man's saying 'No, by God' and 'Yes, by God.'" It has also been read: yurid with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, from wurūd (coming), and its meaning is: whoever comes into it with deviation, wrongfully. From al-Ḥasan: "and whoever intends its deviation with wrongdoing"; he meant "a deviation in it," and annexed it by way of extension in the adverbial, as in "the scheming of the night." Its meaning is: whoever wants to deviate in it, wrongfully. The predicate of inna is omitted, since the answer to the condition indicates it; the implied meaning is: "Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, We will make them taste of a painful punishment," and everyone who commits a sin in it is the same. From Ibn Masʿūd: a mere intention in the Sanctuary is recorded as a sin.
ويؤتون لؤلؤا، كقوله: وحورا عينا. ولؤلوا بقلب الهمزة الثانية واوا. ولوليا، بقلبهما واوين، ثم بقلب الثانية ياء كأدل. ولول كأدل فيمن جرّ. ولولؤ. وليليا، بقلبهما ياءين، عن ابن عباس: وهداهم الله وألهمهم أن يقولوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده، وهداهم إلى طريق الجنة. يقال: فلان يحسن إلى الفقراء وينعش المضطهدين، لا يراد حال ولا استقبال، وإنما يراد استمرار وجود الإحسان منه والنعشة في جميع أزمنته وأوقاته. ومنه قوله تعالى وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أى الصدود منهم مستمرّ دائم لِلنَّاسِ أى الذين يقع عليهم اسم الناس من غير فرق بين حاضر وباد وتانئ «1» وطارئ ومكي وآفاقى. وقد استشهد به أصحاب أبى حنيفة قائلين: إنّ المراد بالمسجد الحرام: مكة، على امتناع جواز بيع دور مكة وإجارتها. وعند الشافعي: لا يمتنع ذلك. وقد حاور إسحاق بن راهويه فاحتجّ بقوله الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ وقال أنسب الديار إلى مالكيها، أو غير مالكيها؟ واشترى عمر بن الخطاب رضى الله تعالى عنه دار السجن من مالكيه أو غير مالكيه؟ سَواءً بالنصب: قراءة حفص. والباقون على الرفع. ووجه النصب أنه ثانى مفعولي جعلناه، أى: جعلناه مستويا الْعاكِفُ فِيهِ وَالْبادِ وفي القراءة بالرفع. الجملة مفعول ثان. الإلحاد: العدول عن القصد، وأصله إلحاد الحافر. وقوله بِإِلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ حالان مترادفتان. ومفعول يُرِدْ متروك ليتناول كل متناول، كأنه قال: ومن يرد فيه مرادا ما عادلا عن القصد ظالما نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ يعنى أنّ الواجب على من كان فيه أن يضبط نفسه ويسلك طريق السداد والعدل في جميع ما يهمّ به ويقصده. وقيل: الإلحاد في الحرم: منع الناس عن عمارته وعن سعيد بن جبير: الاحتكار. وعن عطاء: قول الرجل في المبايعة «لا والله، وبلى والله» وعن عبد الله بن عمر أنه كان له فسطاطان، أحدهما: في الحل، والآخر في الحرم، فإذا أراد أن يعاتب أهله عاتبهم في الحل، «2» فقيل له، فقال، كنا نحدث أن من الإلحاد فيه أن يقول الرجل: لا والله، وبلى والله. وقرئ: يرد، بفتح الياء من الورود. ومعناه: من أتى فيه بإلحاد ظالما. وعن الحسن: ومن يرد إلحاده بظلم، أراد: إلحادا فيه، فأضافه على الاتساع في الظرف، كمكر الليل. ومعناه: من يرد أن يلحد فيه ظالما. وخبر إن محذوف لدلالة جواب الشرط عليه، تقديره: إن الذين كفروا ويصدون عن المسجد الحرام نذيقهم من عذاب أليم، وكل من ارتكب فيه ذنبا فهو كذلك. عن ابن مسعود: الهمة في الحرم تكتب ذنبا.
Vol. 3, p. 152

1. (1). His word "tāniʾ": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: tanaʾtu bi-l-balad tunūʾan means "I dwelt in the town," and al-nātiʾ derives from that. (ʿ)
2. . Transmitted by al-Ṭabarī and al-Azraqī in Tārīkh Makka from the transmission of Shuʿba from Manṣūr from Mujāhid, who said: "ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ had..." and he mentioned it. Note: what appears in the manuscripts of al-Kashshāf, "Ibn ʿUmar," is a scribal corruption; it is only "Ibn ʿAmr".
1. (1) . قوله «وتانئ» في الصحاح: تنأت بالبلد تنوءا: قطنته. والناتئ من ذلك. (ع)
2. . أخرجه الطبري والأزرقى في تاريخ مكة من رواية شعبة عن منصور عن مجاهد قال «كان لعبد الله بن عمرو ابن العاص
…. فذكره» . «تنبيه» ما في نسخ الكشاف «ابن عمر» تصحيف، وإنما هو «ابن عمرو» .
Vol. 3, p. 152
1. (1). His word "al-awthān": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-wathan is the idol. (ʿ)
2. . Transmitted by al-Thaʿlabī from al-Ḥasan, who mentioned it; his chain to him is at the beginning of the book.
3. . Transmitted by al-Ṭabarī from Ibn ʿAbbās with the wording: "He stood at the Stone (al-Ḥijr)," and in one report, "at his station (maqām), and said: 'O people, perform the pilgrimage to the House of your Lord,' and they answered him: 'At Your service, O God, at Your service.'"
4. . His statement "deep in depth and maʿq": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-maʿq is the inversion of al-ʿumq, and al-imʿāq is like al-aʿmāq, which are the remote edges of desert expanses. (ʿ)
1. (1) . قوله «والأوثان» في الصحاح «الوثن» : الصنم. (ع)
2. . أخرجه الثعلبي عن الحسن فذكره. وسنده إليه في أول الكتاب.
3. . أخرجه الطبري عن ابن عباس، بلفظ «قام عند الحجر» وفي رواية «عند مقامه. وقال: يا أيها الناس حجوا بيت ربكم فأجابوه لبيك اللهم لبيك»
4. . قوله «بعيدة العمق والمعق» في الصحاح «المعق» : قلب العمق، والامعاق: مثل الاعماق، وهو ما بعد من أطراف المفاوز. (ع)

Q 22:26 · Vol. 3, p. 152

Verse 26

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And [mention] when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], 'Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who circle it and those who stand and those who bow and prostrate.'" (26)
وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنا لِإِبْراهِيمَ مَكانَ الْبَيْتِ أَنْ لا تُشْرِكْ بِي شَيْئاً وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّائِفِينَ وَالْقائِمِينَ وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ (26)
Vol. 3, p. 152
And remember when We made for Abraham the site of the House a place of settlement (mabāʾa), that is, a place to which one returns, for building and worship. The House had been raised to the heaven in the days of the Flood, and it was of red ruby; God informed Abraham of its site by a wind He sent, called al-Khajūj, which swept clean what was around it, and he built it on its ancient foundation. "That" (an) here is the explanatory.
واذكر حين جعلنا لِإِبْراهِيمَ مَكانَ الْبَيْتِ مباءة، أى: مرجعا يرجع إليه للعمارة والعبادة. رفع البيت إلى السماء أيام الطوفان وكان من ياقوتة حمراء، فأعلم الله إبراهيم مكانه بريح أرسلها يقال لها الخجوج: كنست ما حوله، فبناه على أسه القديم. وأن هي المفسرة.
Question
If you ask: how can the prohibition of association and the command to purify the House be an explanation of the designation?
فإن قلت: كيف يكون النهى عن الشرك والأمر بتطهير البيت تفسيرا للتبوئة؟
Answer
I say: the designation was intended for the sake of worship, so it is as though it were said: "We charged Abraham with worship; We said to him: 'Do not associate anything with Me, and purify My House'" of idols and images (1) and of filth being thrown around it. It has also been read yushrik, with yāʾ, in the third person.
قلت: كانت التبوئة مقصودة من أجل العبادة، فكأنه قيل: تعبدنا إبراهيم قلنا له: لا تُشْرِكْ بِي شَيْئاً وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِيَ من الأصنام والأوثان «1» والأقذار أن تطرح حوله. وقرئ: يشرك، بالياء على الغيبة.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 152

2. . Transmitted by al-Thaʿlabī from al-Ḥasan, who mentioned it; his chain to him is at the beginning of the book.
3. . Transmitted by al-Ṭabarī from Ibn ʿAbbās with the wording: "He stood at the Stone (al-Ḥijr)," and in one report, "at his station (maqām), and said: 'O people, perform the pilgrimage to the House of your Lord,' and they answered him: 'At Your service, O God, at Your service.'"
4. . His statement "deep in depth and maʿq": in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, al-maʿq is the inversion of al-ʿumq, and al-imʿāq is like al-aʿmāq, which are the remote edges of desert expanses. (ʿ)
